title: Large-scale transcriptomic analyses reveal blood biomarker of post-traumatic stress disorder/major depression using weighted gene co-expression network analysis and random forest classifier
description: The primary goal of this study was to identify blood biomarkers of post-traumatic stress disorders. To do so, we generated a large-scale transcriptomic coexpression network, controlling for batch and other covariates, from 466 peripheral blood samples obtained from South Africa. By analyzing the correlations between co-expressed gene communities and multiple traits relevant to PTSD/depression, we were able to identify four modules which were strongly associated with PTSD/depression related traits such as post experiences in childhood trauma, intimate partner violence, lifetime adverse events as well as beck depression inventory (BDI). To further nominate gene candidates that synergistically influence different PTSD/depression relevant traits, hub genes were retrieved from each associated module and overlapped with differential expression, thereby selecting a total of 51 candidate transcripts for downstream analysis. For the validation step, we applied these gene candidates, in conjunction with gene features identified by the Boruta variable selection method, to a random forest (RF) classification model to predict whether subjects could be classified to have post-traumatic stress disorders or not. Different resampling strategies were explored to address the issue of imbalanced data between healthy controls and patients diagnosed with PTSD or depression, of which we found the RF model using down-sampling strategy reached the best performance compared with other resampling RF models. Finally, we were able to verify 14 diagnostic gene markers and clarify the potential clinal utility of peripheral blood gene expression in predicting post-traumatic stress disorders.
